title: Why Package Digital Twins Are So Hard To Build
gist: Package digital twins are harder than fab process twins because they must span silicon, substrate, materials, assembly, test and system operation across multiple companies that each hold pieces of the data as intellectual property. The binding problems are missing context in supplier handoffs, material properties that drift with cure and temperature, non-separable coupled physics, and calibration that expires whenever the application moves outside the validated envelope — making continuous recalibration, not one-time accuracy, the measure of success.

themes.theme: Why package twins differ from fab process twins

insights.claim: A chiplet that is fully characterized, tested and considered known good gives no guarantee it will stay that way after placement into a different package, because a different substrate alters the mechanical and electrical environment, a different thermal interface changes how heat leaves, and a new power envelope changes how much heat must leave.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Undermines the core chiplet reuse economics thesis — die-level qualification does not transfer across package contexts, adding hidden cost per SKU.
insights.quote: The chiplet has not changed, but its electrical, thermal, and mechanical environment has.

insights.claim: A thermal path that worked in a first product can cause throttling in a second product built from the same chiplet, because the surrounding package and cooling assumptions have changed.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Performance regressions from package reuse are a real product risk, which is why per-SKU thermal modeling spend is rising.
insights.quote: A thermal path that worked in the first product can cause throttling in the second because the surrounding package and cooling assumptions have changed.

insights.claim: The distinction is not that fab twins are easy and package twins are hard — a fab process twin is extremely complex, but it lives deep within one manufacturing environment, one process technology, and one managed flow of equipment, materials, process data and statistical learning.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Explains why front-end digital twin vendors' success does not translate directly into the packaging market — different problem structure, different buyers.
insights.quote: A fab twin is usually deep within one manufacturing environment, one process technology, and one managed flow of equipment, materials, process data, and statistical learning.
insights.locator: Fab vs. packaging: A different kind of twin

insights.claim: A package digital twin must solve a broader integration problem — how a multi-die system is realized across silicon, substrate, assembly, manufacturing variation, test and reliability learning — rather than model one process deeply.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Defines the scope a credible package twin product must cover, a useful filter for evaluating EDA and PLM vendor claims.
insights.quote: A package digital twin has to solve a broader integration problem — how a multi-die system is realized across silicon, substrate, assembly, manufacturing variation, test, and reliability learning.
insights.locator: Fab vs. packaging: A different kind of twin

insights.claim: Effective domain tools for electrical, thermal and mechanical behavior do not become a package twin simply by running next to one another; the harder problem is keeping them synchronized around the same physical package as it moves from design to manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Vendors bundling existing point tools are not delivering a twin — synchronization and data plumbing is the differentiated hard part.
insights.quote: Engineers already have effective tools for each of those domains, but they don’t become a package twin simply by running next to one another.
insights.locator: Fab vs. packaging: A different kind of twin

insights.claim: If package, silicon, substrate, materials, thermal solution and manufacturing assumptions are optimized separately, the digital twin degenerates into a late-stage validation artifact, which is not where the value is.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: The ROI case for package twins depends on early co-optimization adoption, not on adding another sign-off checkpoint.
insights.quote: If they are optimized separately, the digital twin becomes a late-stage validation artifact. That is not where the value is.
insights.locator: Fab vs. packaging: A different kind of twin

insights.claim: An end-to-end package digital twin requires visibility across the entire lifecycle from wafer fabrication through assembly, test and ultimately system operation, because key process information originates upstream in foundry operations or downstream in customer applications.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: The required data span crosses at least three company boundaries, making the twin an ecosystem governance problem as much as a software one.
insights.quote: An end-to-end package digital twin requires visibility across the entire lifecycle, from wafer fabrication through assembly, test, and ultimately system operation
insights.locator: Fab vs. packaging: A different kind of twin — Ahn quote

themes.theme: The data hole: missing context across company boundaries

insights.claim: For OSATs an end-to-end digital twin is not a single model but a connected ecosystem of process, equipment, production, supply chain and traceability data, and even equipment inside the same manufacturing flow may provide different types of data depending on its age and supplier.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous installed tool fleets mean data normalization is a persistent operating cost for OSATs, favoring larger players who can fund it.
insights.quote: For OSATs, an end-to-end digital twin is not a single model, but a connected ecosystem of process, equipment, production, supply chain, and traceability data

insights.claim: What an OSAT actually receives falls short of what a predictive model needs: incoming die data may include critical dimensions and wafer-sort results but not detailed power-density or local stress maps, a substrate may arrive within nominal specifications without showing actual warpage across the production lot, and material data sheets may not capture behavior in the end device.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Names the exact data gaps that would have to be closed contractually before package twins can be predictive rather than descriptive.
insights.quote: A substrate may arrive within nominal specifications without showing actual warpage across the production lot

insights.claim: Downstream analysis can look precise while missing manufacturing reality, because what is missing is not just more data but the context telling the next tool or team how the data should be used.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Precision without provenance is a false-confidence trap — a reason to discount vendor accuracy claims that do not address context transfer.
insights.quote: The downstream analysis can then look precise while missing the manufacturing reality.

insights.claim: The hardest handoffs are not where there is least data but where data must move between very different engineering domains — a foundry describing die behavior one way, a substrate supplier another, and a materials company providing properties measured under a very specific set of conditions.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Redirects investment from data collection to semantic translation between domains, a different and less commoditized capability.
insights.quote: The hardest handoffs aren’t necessarily where we have the least data. They’re usually where the data has to move between very different engineering domains

insights.claim: Much of the knowledge needed for a package twin is intellectual property held by separate companies — the material supplier knows chemistry the equipment company does not, and the equipment company knows process integration details unavailable to the OSAT or fab.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: IP protection is a structural, not technical, barrier — implying either consortium-style data agreements or vendor-neutral intermediaries become necessary.
insights.quote: We all have our own data and everybody wants to protect intellectual property.

insights.claim: The industry was formerly more open in how it collaborated as an ecosystem, and that shift toward guarded data is now a drag on building package twins.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Suggests the bottleneck could ease through commercial norms shifting rather than new technology — a slower but real catalyst to watch.
insights.quote: I’ve been in this industry all my life, and when we started we had a different way of collaborating. We were a lot more open as an industry, as an ecosystem.

insights.claim: A common file format can move information between tools but cannot supply process data that was never shared, a material property that was never characterized, or an upstream excursion never attached to the incoming die — meaning the model can be incomplete before the first coupled simulation runs.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations for standards-driven solutions to the packaging data problem; format standardization is necessary but far from sufficient.
insights.quote: A common file format can help move information between tools, but it can’t provide process data that was never shared

themes.theme: As-drawn versus as-manufactured: process variation defeats idealized models

insights.claim: Photonic devices are typically designed and optimized using idealized geometries while manufactured devices are governed by process-induced variability, so a design optimized for the as-drawn geometry often does not represent the as-manufactured device.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Explains why silicon photonics struggles to move from lab demos to high-volume manufacturing — a recurring risk for optical interconnect roadmaps.
insights.quote: The biggest disconnect is that photonic devices are typically designed and optimized using idealized geometries, while manufactured devices are governed by process-induced variability
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Guichard quote

insights.claim: In photonics, critical dimensions, film thickness or sidewall profile can shift enough during processing to change optical loss or wavelength response without anything being obviously broken.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Silent parametric degradation makes photonics yield harder to detect and fix than digital logic yield, raising qualification cost.
insights.quote: Critical dimensions, film thickness, or sidewall profile can move enough during processing to change optical loss or wavelength response without anything being obviously “broken.”

insights.claim: Fine process details such as humidity levels, changes in cleaning chemistry concentration, or a slight under-etch must become explicit model inputs if they change performance.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: The input space for a credible package twin expands into fab housekeeping variables, which vastly increases required instrumentation.

insights.claim: ASIC design tools set an expectation that simulation output closely matches the software model, but that correlation breaks down for technologies that lack comparable lifetime and qualification history or that push the bleeding edge, where subtleties can have massive impacts.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Explains why simulation-first design economics do not transfer to novel packaging and photonics — physical build cycles remain mandatory and costly.
insights.quote: Subtle nuances don’t show up in the model.
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Booth quote

insights.claim: Introducing any new material explodes the number of knobs and dials, because engineers must know how the material performs across many different environments and what its variance is over its lifetime.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Quantifies the hidden qualification tax on novel packaging materials, which slows adoption regardless of the material's headline properties.
insights.quote: When you introduce any new material into that, it just explodes the number of knobs and dials
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Booth quote

themes.theme: Material properties as moving targets, not datasheet constants

insights.claim: A datasheet gives only a snapshot of CTE, modulus, adhesion and viscosity measured under one set of conditions at one point in time, while mechanical and thermal properties shift with the degree of curing and crosslink density may continue to evolve after processing.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Datasheet-driven simulation systematically misrepresents materials, which is the root of documented simulation-to-silicon gaps.
insights.quote: A datasheet gives you a snapshot — CTE, modulus, adhesion, viscosity, measured under one set of conditions at one point in time.
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Chen quote

insights.claim: CTE varies particularly in the temperature region near a polymer's glass transition temperature, and treating any of these properties as a single static number causes a lot of simulation-to-silicon gaps.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Names the specific physics region where package models break, guiding where characterization investment actually pays off.
insights.quote: Treating any of these as a single static number causes a lot of simulation-to-silicon gaps.
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Chen quote

insights.claim: Adhesion strength depends heavily on the specific bonding interface, so a material value that was accurate when a model was built can become less representative after cure, thermal exposure or assembly even when the material name and formulation have not changed.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Model validity decays through the process flow itself, requiring versioned material data rather than a static library.
insights.quote: Crosslink density may continue to evolve after processing, and adhesion strength depends heavily on the specific bonding interface.
insights.locator: Manufacturing gets a vote — Chen quote

themes.theme: Coupled physics and the interface standardization gap

insights.claim: Engineers may model thermal, mechanical and electrical behavior separately for expediency, but the physical package does not respect those boundaries — current creates heat, heat changes resistance, electrical changes alter dissipated power, and the new power distribution changes the thermal picture again, forcing iteration until results converge.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Coupled-loop convergence is a compute-intensive requirement that raises the cost and runtime of package sign-off, benefiting multiphysics tool vendors.
insights.quote: Current creates heat, heat changes resistance, and those electrical changes alter the power being dissipated.

insights.claim: Process variables rarely act independently, and yield is often limited by the combined and nonlinear interaction of multiple process variations rather than by any single variation.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Nonlinear interaction means yield improvement cannot be decomposed into independent fixes — a driver of statistical, multi-variable modeling tools.
insights.quote: Yield is often limited by the combined and nonlinear interaction of multiple process variations.
insights.locator: When one problem becomes another — Guichard quote

insights.claim: The least-standardized models are at the interfaces rather than in the isolated physics domains, in the difficult areas where materials, structures, processes, suppliers and system-level decisions meet.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Points standards bodies and tool vendors at interface assumptions as the highest-value unsolved area in packaging modeling.
insights.quote: The least-standardized models are often at the interfaces, not in the isolated physics domains.
insights.locator: When one problem becomes another — Larsen quote

insights.claim: A substrate supplier and an assembly house can both hold technically valid models that describe different parts of the same physical behavior under different assumptions, so the failure is not that either model is wrong but that they do not mesh into a common representation of the package.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Reconciliation of valid-but-incompatible models is a distinct product opportunity separate from building better physics solvers.

themes.theme: Calibration as a continuous process with expiry

insights.claim: In Intel's hybrid-bonding work, experimental distortion data is fed back into the finite-element model so engineers can refine it and then use it to explore changes that would be impractical to test experimentally.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: A working template for measurement-fed model refinement in the most demanding advanced packaging process now moving toward volume.
insights.quote: Experimental distortion data is fed back into the finite-element model, which engineers can then refine before using it to explore changes that would be impractical to test experimentally.

insights.claim: The answer is not to measure everything at every step but to measure at the points where the package changes state — transitions including bonding, molding, curing, thinning and thermal transitions.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: A metrology placement heuristic that defines where inspection spend in advanced packaging lines will concentrate.
insights.quote: I don’t think the answer is to measure everything at every step. It’s really about measuring at the points where the package changes state.

insights.claim: Warpage is the obvious calibration measurement for a package model but is not enough; the calibration set has to include bump and interconnect metrology, die placement, substrate characterization, underfill/mold/TIM measurements, thermal characterization and electrical testing.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Enumerates the full metrology basket a package twin demands — a direct read on advanced packaging inspection equipment demand.
insights.quote: For a package model, warpage is the obvious measurement, but it is not enough.

insights.claim: Model development and physical development cannot be separated when the technology is new — the twin has to be built at the same time as the devices, in lockstep, because a digital twin cannot be called accurate until a part has actually been built and correlated.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Kills the hope that twins reduce prototype builds for emerging technology; they add parallel effort before they save any.
insights.quote: You’ve got to build that twin at the same time you’re building the devices, so you have some correlation

insights.claim: There is no fixed recalibration interval — it is driven by how far the new application sits from the conditions of the original model, with a new package architecture, a different substrate, a shift in thermal budget or a change in process flow all capable of moving a material outside its validated envelope.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Recalibration becomes a recurring, application-triggered service revenue stream for materials suppliers rather than a scheduled cost.
insights.quote: There’s no fixed interval; it’s driven by how far the new application sits from the conditions of the original model

insights.claim: Reduced-order and AI surrogate models gain speed by using a simplified representation, and without the context of the conditions under which they remain trustworthy, a fast model becomes a fast way to make the wrong decision.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: A direct caution on AI-accelerated simulation in packaging — validity metadata, not model speed, is the differentiator worth paying for.
insights.quote: Without that context, a fast model can become a fast way to make the wrong decision.

insights.claim: In advanced packaging there may never be a point when everything is completely known, because components come from different suppliers, materials change during processing, and assembly introduces new stresses and interactions — so the twin must evolve with the package or become a precise model of something that no longer exists.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Frames package twins as a subscription-like ongoing capability rather than a deliverable, reshaping how the software should be priced and staffed.
insights.quote: The twin has to evolve along with the package or risk becoming a precise model of something that no longer exists.
insights.locator: Conclusion: Keeping the twin attached to reality

insights.claim: The real measure of success is not predicting the physical package perfectly once, but remaining useful as the physical package changes — with the built package improving the model and the model letting teams ask what will change before committing to the next design, package stack or product SKU.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Supplies the evaluation criterion buyers should apply to package twin offerings, replacing one-shot accuracy benchmarks.
insights.quote: A useful package twin is not just a simulation sitting next to the hardware.
insights.locator: Conclusion: Keeping the twin attached to reality
